home.faq_heading: Frequently asked questions about the integration exam
home.faq_subheading: Everything you need to know before you start practising
home.faq_q1: Which parts does the integration exam have?
home.faq_a1: You take four language parts: Reading, Listening, Writing and Speaking. You also take KNM (Knowledge of Dutch Society) and ONA. This platform covers the language parts at A2 and at B1, plus KNM. Only Listening B1 and ONA are still on the way.
home.faq_q2: How many tasks does each language part have?
home.faq_a2: At A2, Reading and Listening each have 25 multiple-choice questions with three options (A, B or C). Writing has 4 writing tasks and Speaking has 16 speaking tasks.
home.faq_q3: How long do the exams take?
home.faq_a3: At A2, Reading takes about 65 minutes, Listening 45, Writing 40 and Speaking 35. Our practice exams use the same timings, so you know how it feels.
home.faq_q4: How are Writing and Speaking graded?
home.faq_a4: Your answer is graded against the marking rubric our NT2 teacher wrote herself: you get a score per criterion with an explanation. The teacher reviews those gradings and adjusts the rubric where needed. So the rubric comes from a teacher, not from a model.
home.faq_a5: Practice exam 1 of every part is free and complete — not a sample, a full exam. You need no account for it. All 40 practice exams of a level need a paid subscription.
home.faq_q6: Are the tasks made by AI?
home.faq_a6: No. Every task is written or reviewed by a certified NT2 teacher before it goes live. For Writing and Speaking a model helps apply the rubric, but the rubric, the model answers and the review all come from the teacher.

inburgering.meta_title: Integrating in the Netherlands: the steps explained
inburgering.meta_description: How does integrating in the Netherlands work? Which exams you take, what it costs and which law applies to you — explained simply, with every source named.
inburgering.heading: Integrating in the Netherlands, explained
inburgering.subheading: What you have to do, in what order, and where you can check it yourself. Every figure in these guides has a source.
inburgering.intro_body: Inburgering means learning Dutch and learning how the Netherlands works. You take exams at DUO. Pass them all and you get your diploma. Exactly which exams you take depends on your personal plan (PIP) and your learning route.
inburgering.phase_1_body: It states the date from which your integration period runs.
inburgering.phase_2_title: Your municipality makes a PIP with you
inburgering.phase_2_body: It sets out your learning route and which exams you take.
inburgering.phase_3_body: Usually with lessons at a language school, plus practice on your own.
inburgering.phase_4_body: Each component is a separate exam, on a separate day.
inburgering.phase_5_body: Failed one component? You retake only that one.

knm.meta_title: KNM: knowledge of Dutch society, explained
knm.meta_description: KNM is the exam component about how the Netherlands works: housing, work, healthcare, education and social customs. Here is what it is and how to prepare.
knm.heading: KNM: knowledge of Dutch society
knm.subheading: The exam component that is not about language, but about how the Netherlands works day to day.
knm.intro_body: KNM asks about living in the Netherlands: housing, work, healthcare, education, money and dealing with other people. You watch short clips and look at photos, then choose the answer that fits. It is a separate exam component, alongside the four language ones.
knm.phase_1_body: Renting, waste, noise and getting along with neighbours.
knm.phase_2_body: Applying for jobs, contracts, tax and insurance.
knm.phase_3_body: The GP, the pharmacy and how Dutch healthcare is arranged.
knm.phase_4_body: School, compulsory education and talking to your child’s teacher.
knm.phase_5_body: Making appointments, being on time and how people talk to each other.

taalexamens.meta_title: Dutch integration language exams: the 4 components
taalexamens.meta_description: Reading, listening, writing and speaking at A2 and B1: what each component requires, how long each exam takes, and how to practise for it properly.
taalexamens.intro_body: The language part of your integration consists of four exams. You take them separately, on different days. Reading and listening are multiple-choice on a computer. For writing you produce short texts yourself, and for speaking you record your answers. Each component asks something different of you, so you prepare for each one differently.
taalexamens.phase_1_body: You read short everyday texts: a letter, an email, an advert or a form. Then you answer questions about them.
taalexamens.phase_2_body: You hear conversations and short announcements, such as a phone call or a public announcement, and answer questions about what you heard.
taalexamens.phase_3_body: You fill in a form and write short texts, such as an email or a note. This component is marked by people.
taalexamens.phase_4_body: You record your answers at a computer. You respond to questions and describe what you see in a picture.

eu_citizen.title: You usually do not have to integrate
eu_citizen.body: If you come from the EU, the EEA or Switzerland, the inburgering obligation usually does not apply to you. Do you still want to learn Dutch or apply for naturalisation? Then you take the exams voluntarily.

under_18.title: You usually do not have to integrate
under_18.body: If you are under 18 and still of compulsory school age, the obligation usually does not apply. You go to school and learn Dutch there.

pension_age.title: You usually do not have to integrate
pension_age.body: If you have reached state pension age, the inburgering obligation usually does not apply to you.

temporary_stay.title: You usually do not have to integrate
temporary_stay.body: If you are in the Netherlands temporarily for work or study, the obligation usually does not apply. If you stay longer or your reason for staying changes, that can change too.

permit_holder.title: The obligation probably applies to you
permit_holder.body: Based on your answers the obligation applies. DUO sends you a letter about it. That letter carries a date, and the date decides which act applies to you — that is your next step.

need_more.title: We cannot say yet
need_more.body: With these answers it is not certain. The good news: you do not have to work it out yourself. DUO decides and sends you a letter. Below you can read how to check it.

knm_woorden.title: KNM vocabulary: the words you need to know
knm_woorden.intro: KNM uses words you rarely hear in daily life: huurcontract, zorgverzekering, gemeenteraad. Here is where you will practise them.
knm_woorden.what_1: You practise the words by KNM theme, so you learn them in the context you will meet them in the exam.
knm_woorden.what_2: Each word comes with its article, its plural, an explanation in simple Dutch and an example sentence.
knm_woorden.what_3: Not sure about a word? You can read the explanation in English, Arabic or Turkish.
knm_woorden.built_from: The words already exist: they are in this project, organised by KNM theme, with translations. They only need the teacher’s review before they appear here.

taal_woorden.title: Exam vocabulary: words per component
taal_woorden.intro: Which words keep coming back in the reading, listening, writing and speaking exams? We are putting them together here.
taal_woorden.what_1: You practise the words per component and per level, so A2 and B1 separately.
taal_woorden.what_2: Each word comes with an example sentence in the style of the exam, so you learn it in the right context.
taal_woorden.what_3: You can use the list to check what you already know and practise only the words you do not.
taal_woorden.built_from: The list comes from the practice exams on this site: the words the teacher actually uses in her tasks, not a generic frequency list.

taal_woorden.meta_description: Practise the vocabulary of the A2 and B1 language exams for free, organised per component, each with an example sentence in the style of the real exam.

grammatica.title: Grammar: only what you need for the exam
grammatica.intro: You do not need all of Dutch grammar to pass. Here we explain which rules actually come back in the exam.
grammatica.what_1: For each rule you get a short explanation in simple Dutch, with examples from real exam tasks.
grammatica.what_2: You see the mistakes students make most often in writing and speaking, and how to avoid them.
grammatica.what_3: For every rule you can do a few exercises straight away, so you find out whether you really understand it.
grammatica.built_from: The topics are chosen from the mistakes the teacher sees in her marking — the grammar that costs points, not the grammar a textbook happens to cover.
grammatica.meta_title: Integration exam grammar: the rules that really come back
grammatica.meta_description: Which Dutch grammar do you need for the integration exam? A short explanation per rule, with examples and the mistakes students make most often.

tijdlijn.meta_title: Integration timeline: when do you have to register?
tijdlijn.meta_description: You have 3 years to complete integration. But registering takes over 6 weeks and results take 8 to 16. Work out the last safe date to register for your final exam.

hero.title: When do you have to do what?
hero.sub: You have 3 years to complete your integration. But registering for an exam often takes more than 6 weeks, and the result another 8 to 16. So your real last moment is months before your deadline. This tool works out when that is.
hero.privacy: No DigiD. No BSN. Your answers stay on your own phone.
hero.meta_line: 6 questions · about 2 minutes · no account needed
hero.how_1: The date by which you must register for your final exam.
hero.how_2: For each part: when you can start, what it costs and who pays.
hero.how_3: Your timeline as a PDF, or by email, so you can keep it with your DUO papers.
hero.trust_title: Why you can trust these dates
hero.trust_body: Every figure says where it came from and when we checked it. Our own estimates are shown separately, with dashed lines and the word about. So you can always see which number comes from DUO and which comes from us.

q1.title: Where are you right now?
q1.sub: This tells us which questions we still need to ask you.
q1.abroad: I don't live in the Netherlands yet
q1.abroad_note: Then your term has not started.
q1.arrived: I just arrived, I have no letter yet
q1.arrived_note: Your clock is not running yet. We show you what is coming.
q1.letter: I have a letter from DUO or a PIP
q1.letter_note: Then we can work out your real dates.
q1.busy: I have been at this for a while
q1.busy_note: We check whether you are going to make it.
q1.over_note: We show what happens now and how much time you get.
q1.passport: I don't have to, but I want a Dutch passport
q1.passport_note: Then we build a naturalisation timeline.

q2.title: When did your integration term start?
q2.sub: First choose which document you have. Then the month and the year.
q2.pip_note: Your term starts the day after the date on your first PIP.
q2.letter_note: That letter says from when you must integrate.
q2.gemeente: Neither — but I know when I registered with the municipality
q2.gemeente_note: That is not the same date. We then calculate on the safe side: your real term starts later, so you probably have a little more time than we show.
q2.help_title: Where do I find this date?
q2.help_body: Look at the first page of your PIP or your DUO letter, top right. That is where the dagtekening is: the day the document was issued. Lost the letter? Log in to Mijn Inburgering with your DigiD. It shows which law, which route and which exams apply to you.

q3.title: What is your situation?
q3.sub: This decides who pays for your course and your exams.
q3.asiel: I hold an asylum residence permit
q3.asiel_note: The municipality usually pays your course. Your first 2 attempts per exam are free.
q3.gezin: I came to join my partner or family, or I have another residence permit
q3.gezin_note: You pay yourself, or you borrow from DUO.
q3.eu: I am from the EU, or I don't have to integrate
q3.eu_note: Then you have no term and no fine.

q4.title: Which learning route are you on?
q4.sub: It is in your PIP. Don't know? Then we use the B1 route, because most people are on it.
q4.b1_note: Four language exams at B1, plus KNM, PVT and MAP.
q4.onderwijs_note: You want to go to mbo, hbo or university. B1 or B2.
q4.z_note: Learning is hard. You work toward A1 and finish with an interview at the municipality.
q4.wi2013: I fall under the old law (2013)
q4.wi2013_note: Four language exams at A2, plus KNM, ONA and PVT.

q5.title: What have you already done?
q5.sub: Tap how far you are for each part. You can change this later.

q6.title: How much do you study each week?
q6.sub: We use this to estimate when you are ready for an exam.
q6.self: Hours studying on your own per week
q6.no_course: I don't have a course yet
q6.effective: We calculate with {n} hours per week
q6.effective_note: Hours with a teacher count fully. Studying on your own counts half — that is our own estimate, and it is the cautious side.
q6.level_title: How good is your Dutch now?
q6.level_a2: A2 — I manage in daily life
q6.level_b1: B1 — I can hold a conversation

q7.title: Two more things
q7.sub: These two questions can save you months.
q7.passport_title: Do you want to become Dutch later?
q7.passport_note: Then we put the passport clock next to it: 5 years living in the Netherlands and your diploma.
q7.residence_title: Since which year have you lived in the Netherlands?
q7.signals_title: Has anything happened that cost you time?
q7.signals_note: We use this to see whether you might get extra time. DUO decides that, not us.
q7.sig_literacy: I had to learn to read and write first
q7.sig_illness: Illness, mine or someone in my family
q7.sig_homeless: I had no home, or I was in a shelter
q7.sig_gemeente: The municipality or my school did not arrange things in time
q7.extension_title: Has DUO already given you extra time?

q_residence.title: Since when have you lived in the Netherlands?
q_residence.sub: This lets us draw your timeline even before you have a letter from DUO. It is also the clock for a Dutch passport.

result.because: After that there is no time left for the result to arrive before your deadline on {date}.
result.verdict_on_track: You have room — if you start now.
result.verdict_tight: It is going to be tight. This is the order.
result.verdict_at_risk: At this pace you will not make it.
result.verdict_at_risk_sub: You have two options: start faster, or apply for an extension.
result.verdict_overdue: Your term has ended. Here is what happens now.
result.verdict_pre_clock: Your clock is not running yet. This is what is coming.
result.verdict_naturalisation: Two clocks are running side by side.
result.verdict_estimate: We are working with an estimate.
result.verdict_estimate_sub: Fill in the date on your PIP and you get real dates.
result.next_step_body: {component} is the one you can pass soonest. That gives you breathing room straight away.
result.timeline_sub: From today to your deadline. The solid bar is studying — you decide that. The hatched bar is waiting for DUO.
result.node_diagnostic: Where do you stand now? 10 questions, 3 minutes, no account.
result.cost_sub: The price per exam part is the same for A2 and B1.
result.cost_free_attempts_note: Only if you sit the exam at the level in your PIP, or higher.
result.cost_loan_income: You can borrow from DUO. How much depends on your income. Only at a school listed on zoekinburgerschool.nl.
result.cost_loan_max: You can borrow up to € 10,000 from DUO.
result.cost_loan_none: Note: as an asylum status holder under the 2021 law you cannot borrow from DUO. Your municipality pays for your course.
result.cost_childcare: Do you have children in childcare? Then you can get childcare allowance for your course, MAP, PVT and participation hours. Many people do not know this.
result.cost_naturalisation: Naturalisation costs a further {amount} (single application, rate from 1 January 2026).
result.extension_automatic: You do not have to apply for this. DUO does it itself.
result.extension_apply: You have to apply for this. DUO decides within {n} weeks.
result.extension_all: You tick every box. Check with DUO whether that is right.
result.extension_condition_unknown: I don't know — tick it yourself
result.cond_route_b1: You are on the B1 route (scaling down to A2 does not matter)
result.cond_30_months: Your term started more than 2.5 years ago
result.cond_2_of_4: You passed 2 of the 4 language exams, at the level in your PIP or higher
result.cond_knm_hours: You attended every lesson of the KNM course
result.cond_lessons: You attended every language lesson in your PIP
result.cond_450_hours: You had at least 450 hours of language lessons, plus the KNM hours, at a school with the keurmerk
result.cond_300_hours: You had at least 300 hours of lessons at a school with the Blik op Werk keurmerk
result.cond_ona: You completed ONA in full at least once
result.cond_attempts_twice: You attempted every exam you have not passed at least twice
result.cond_online_excluded: Hours you did online do not count
result.cond_child_born: Your child was born during your term
result.ext_childbirth: Extra time after the birth of your child
result.ext_many_hours: Six months extra because you have done a lot
result.ext_literacy: You had to learn to read and write first
result.ext_gemeente: The municipality or school did not arrange it
result.fine_title: What happens if you are late
result.fine_none_asiel: You hold an asylum residence permit. That means you get no fine. The Raad van State ruled that DUO may not fine asylum status holders for taking too long, and may not reclaim your integration loan. You do have to carry on integrating.
result.fine_max: The fine is at most {amount}. What you actually pay depends on your route, your lesson hours, your attempts and the exams you already passed. Only DUO knows that, so we do not calculate an amount for you.
result.fine_pvt: PVT not completed in time: at most {amount}.
result.fine_map: MAP not completed in time: at most {amount}.
result.fine_extra_time: After a fine you get {n} months extra to finish. Your new end date is then {date}.
result.fine_letter: Two months before the end of your term, DUO sends you a letter with the data it holds. Is something wrong? Then report it straight away.
result.naturalisation_residence: Living in the Netherlands for 5 years
result.naturalisation_binding_residence: Your waiting time for the passport decides when you can apply, not your exams. So you have room to learn.
result.naturalisation_binding_diploma: Your exams decide when you can apply. So start on them now.
result.naturalisation_fee: The application costs {amount} for one person.
result.naturalisation_decision: The IND decides within 1 year. In practice it takes 6 to 9 months.
result.naturalisation_z_route: Note: a Z-route certificate does not let you naturalise. You need an integration diploma, or an advies aantoonbaar geleverde inspanningen. Sort this out before the end of your term, not after.
result.naturalisation_pending: A bill has been proposed to extend these 5 years to 10, and to require B1. That is not law yet. We calculate with today's law.
result.whatif_sub: Change something and see what happens to your dates.
result.whatif_retake: What if I fail one exam?
result.whatif_retake_note: Then a new registration and a new result are added: {n} weeks together.
result.whatif_extension: I have been given extra time
result.save_sub: Your timeline is in the address of this page. Keep it, or send it to yourself.
result.save_email_consent: Also remind me before my last date to register.
result.save_email_privacy: We only keep your email address and your timeline. You can unsubscribe in every email.
result.sources_sub: Every figure from DUO carries its source and the day we checked it. Our own estimates are listed separately.
result.sources_needs_confirmation: still to be verified at the source itself
result.sources_planning_body: How many hours you need for a level, how many weeks you still have to study and how often you will probably sit an exam: those are our estimates, not DUO rules. They are always labelled as estimates and always given as a range.
result.w_not_an_official_decision: This is a tool, not an official decision. DUO decides your term. Check Mijn Inburgering.
result.w_anchor_unknown: You don't know your start date yet. We are working with an estimate. Find the dagtekening on your PIP or your DUO letter, or check Mijn Inburgering — then your dates become real.
result.w_anchor_month_precision: You gave a month, not a day. Your dates can therefore shift by a few weeks.
result.w_anchor_is_gemeente_registration: You gave the date you registered with the municipality. Your term starts later than that. We calculate on the safe side, so you probably have a little more time than shown here.
result.w_law_unknown: We don't know which law applies to you. Check your DUO letter or Mijn Inburgering.
result.w_route_assumed_b1: We are using the B1 route, because most people are on it. Does your PIP say something else? Then change it.
result.w_nt2_result_lead_unknown: For the exams at B1 and B2 we have not yet verified the result waiting time at DUO. For now we calculate with 8 weeks. Bear in mind that it can take longer.
result.w_volatile_16_week_notice: DUO currently states that the result for Speaking A2 and Writing A2 can take up to 16 weeks. That is a temporary notice. We do calculate with it, because it changes your plan considerably.
result.w_z_route_not_enough_for_passport: A Z-route certificate does not let you become Dutch. Read below what you need instead.
result.w_bio_not_enough_for_passport: A dispensation for special individual circumstances is not enough to naturalise.
result.w_asiel_never_fined: You hold an asylum residence permit. You get no fine if you go over your term.
result.w_no_study_hours_given: You have not yet said how much you study each week. That is why we cannot estimate when you will be ready for an exam. Fill it in under "What if things go differently?".
